s6.title: 2974 Walton Robotics 2024 robot, Fusion share link

s8.title: Photo listed on The Blue Alliance

demand.text: The goal was to be an alliance captain at Worlds. In qualifications: every ranking point, from speaker and amp notes, a spotlit climb and wins. At 25 notes (21 with coopertition) they judged cooperation necessary with some partners, and climb plus trap imperative at championships. In playoffs autonomous came first; clearing the field puts up 61 points.

auto.text: Choreo paths followed with PathPlanner on wheel odometry, starting from the center, amp side or source side.
Midline routines came before Carrollton, where they wrote one in eliminations to fit a partner.
Routines grew from three pieces to 3.5, four and five.

cycle.text: One button intakes: the conveyor beam break stops the note and pulls it back from the flywheels. A second button spins up once the note is clear and feeds once spun up and aimed at a preset.
The shooter flips down to force a note into the amp.

endgame.text: Rods flip out to put hooks on the chain, and two winches pull the robot up. For the trap, a two-part arm on the shooter opens the trap door so the shooter can shoot into it.

gave_up.text: Space was left for a climber while note scoring came first. It was designed before Anderson but, still in testing, was not attached until the district championship.
A behind-the-bumper intake means the frame perimeter is not the same as the drive base.
The robot played Anderson and Carrollton without a camera; one went on the shooter after Carrollton, to rely less on preset distances.

changed.text: The conveyor's idler slowed notes and its polybelt melted, so it became guide plates and one belt-driven roller. Winches turned 90 degrees to fit. Notes stuck to the trap door, so a door-opening arm was added.
A stripped pivot belt became chain; later the pivot got GT2 belts and faster gearing.
Being fed at the district championship gave their highest note average, so they moved toward collecting passes and shooting.

outcome.text: 60-6-0 in official play; ranked 17 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 52.79, Newton).

facts.text: SDS MK4i modules, L3 ratio, Kraken drive and Falcon 500 steer
Frame perimeter is 28.5 x 28.5 in
1/8 in aluminum belly plate without pockets
The belly plate changed from a 1/4 in polycarbonate plan to 1/8 in aluminum to give back a little clearance under the chassis

solves.text: Touch it, own it: take a note with a large area of acceptable contact

facts.text: Compression on the note in testing
Two carbon fiber rods with grippy tube rubber, slick tape, one Kraken
Two printed side pieces funnel the note
The wide span lets drivers grab notes without slowing to align, a main reason for quick cycles
Rollers started as polycarbonate with rubber covers and became carbon fiber, lighter and stronger, with bought end adapters
After Anderson split the HDPE note guide above it and damaged its PLA brackets, the guide became polycarbonate with TPU brackets

cost.text: The frame perimeter is not the same as the drive base
Hits at Anderson, especially in playoffs, bowed the tubes above the intake in by up to about a quarter inch; the team calls the front fairly robust and planned identical replacements
A hit at the district championship cracked the side plates; bolt holes limited the crack, and spares went on the next day
At an off-season event in 2024 one side of the intake plate cracked down the middle in auto, and the bumpers held the intake together for the last match

functions.name: Conveyor

solves.text: Carry the note straight from intake to shooter, including uncentered notes

functions.type: guide plates with one powered top roller

facts.text: NEO with a custom gearbox at
18T pulleys and a 55T timing belt; 1/16 in HDPE top and bottom guides
Runs at the same time as the intake, at the shooter's width
The conveyor roller pulls a note fully in once it touches, so off-center intaking works
It was to share power with a shooter roller, but a support added to stop the shooter bowing blocked that polybelt, so it got its own NEO

cost.text: It took several versions: a wheeled idler slowed the note, HDPE bowed, and a polybelt melted and snapped
The polybelt overheated from too much torque and its NEO pulley spun free, so a timing belt and a thicker gearbox replaced it

functions.name: Shooter

solves.text: Shoot every intaken note consistently, with range and accuracy

functions.type: top and bottom dual flywheel shooter

facts.text: Two Falcon 500s with 2:1 speed-up pulleys
85T belts to the top flywheels; a 30T belt and 32T gears to the bottom
Assembly is 20.25 in high and 16.50 in wide
Four carbon fiber feed rollers, NEO at
Guide plates went from HDPE to 1/16 in polycarbonate so drivers see whether the note is centered
The design is inspired by 6328, says a post that corrects an earlier one naming 111

Flipping the shooter down into the amp, after ORBIT, was extremely consistent before its first event; the amp shot was adjusted at Carrollton and lost its aim in one Newton match when a pivot belt skipped
Notes shot in official matches at the championship, about 40 of them into the amp
After Carrollton 1x2 tubes under the flywheels became hex axles to save weight, and camera mounts top and bottom became part of the structure

cost.text: Off-center notes in practice had to be scored from nearly underneath the speaker

solves.text: Move quickly with little backlash while carrying the whole shooter

facts.text: Falcon 500 reduction as the Worlds summary gives it; an earlier post says it had been changed after Carrollton
A 100T belt joins a 24T pulley to a 61T pulley on the shooter side plate; HTD belts were replaced by GT2 after Carrollton to stop skipping and reduce slop
Planned hard stop so the shooter cannot go below
The absolute encoder is coupled to the shooter angle, so gearbox backlash does not affect control
A printed axle attachment rubbing on old tread damps backlash
Reduction after Carrollton, changed from 125:1 for faster rotation; the Worlds summary, posted later, still gives 125:1
The motor end runs on two 31-link #25 chains with 18T sprockets

cost.text: Belts skipped until a tensioner and more tension were added, and a 36T belt stripped and was replaced by chain
The belt repair needed the intake and front modules off, so access holes were added
Slop made drivers wait a couple of seconds after each angle change before firing, so a friction damper was added
At and after Carrollton the right belt had to be skipped with the robot off so the shooter rested evenly on its stops
At Newton a belt skipped when the arm extended; logs of encoder against motor position showed it, and it was tightened

solves.text: Climb as high as possible toward the trap, from parts on hand or easily made, and be easy to attach and remove

facts.text: NEO gearbox
Printed spool, and printed inserts with embedded nuts so it comes off easily
The rods are called bent fiberglass, carbon fiber and 1/4 in polycarbonate in different places of the same summary
Fiberglass rods replaced servos to keep weight off the shooter; after testing, the plan was polycarbonate sheets, to keep the hooks moving in one plane
Printed hooks were to become polycarbonate for strength

cost.text: It was not attached until the district championship, after testing
PLA hook supports broke, so TPU ones were tested
It was left off for Anderson so programming could focus on autos instead of climbing
The mini PC was in the way on one side, so a side plate was cut, a motor moved and the gear ratio changed

functions.name: Trap

solves.text: Open the trap door so a note does not stick to it

functions.type: double actuating arm that opens the trap door

facts.text: The first arm pivots on an axial spring joined to the shooter; the second on an elastic band around a pulley
One arm became two pivots, for the length needed to press on the trap door
The release was first a linear actuator; a rotational servo was to be tested before Worlds

functions.name: Note-tracking state machine

solves.text: Never spin the flywheels on an unready note or feed before they are up to speed

functions.type: photoelectric and beam break sensors driving a state machine

facts.text: An intake sensor finishes the intake even if the driver lets go early
A conveyor beam break stops the intake and pulls the note back slightly
A shooter beam break confirms the note has left
Controllers rumble to show where the note is
Code logs the time from a shot request to the note leaving or the request ending

solves.text: Shed notes that fall on the chassis and protect the top of the intake and conveyor

facts.text: Added the week of Anderson; the team credits it in part for no major mechanical problems there, though hits bowed front tubes and damaged bumper brackets

solves.text: Let notes pass under without a low section that would anchor a tip

facts.text: Height above the ground is listed as 2 1/4, with no unit printed
Seams are on the sides, to reinforce the front of the frame
Spacers later raised them to leave more clearance for the note

solves.text: Rely less on lining up the drive base at preset distances

facts.text: A See3CAM_24CUG at the center of the shooter; its mount replaced aluminum bars between the flywheels and is part of the structure
The mount is based on 111's, and the plan was to use it in auto and teleop
Wheel radius is measured by a routine inspired by 6328, which the team finds much easier than pushing the robot and measuring

cost.text: At Anderson the robot slipped off Choreo paths, which do not account for battery voltage; limiting the torque more fixed it

decisions.because: it was the most efficient intake tested, with an ideal angle into the robot and the full frame width
decisions.instead_of: stacked rollers over the bumper, which conveyed poorly and lost time flipping out, or an under-chassis intake
decisions.cost: the frame perimeter is not the same as the drive base

decisions.because: notes went much further than with side rollers
decisions.instead_of: a side-roller shooter, which lacked range by calculation and by test
decisions.cost: the prototype, which used Colson wheels, was very heavy, which raised pivoting concerns

decisions.because: it could be fitted to the finished intake and shooter

decisions.choice: Extend the intake instead of a full conveyor (January plan; a powered conveyor roller came later)
decisions.because: the full conveyor prototype was a bit slower and tore the note slightly
note scoring came first because the game was complex
raising both wrists or turning to shoot would take too much time in auto
it costs less and is easier for drivers to notice
a lower C-shape would be an anchor for tipping over
decisions.instead_of: a C-shaped bumper lower than the front piece

decisions.choice: Lock the shooter re-zero behind three buttons
decisions.because: drivers re-zeroed it by accident in a match
it can bring the bottom of the robot as close to the chain as possible
decisions.instead_of: climbing by lowering the shooter onto the chain

decisions.choice: Climb by lowering the shooter onto the chain (January plan, later dropped)
decisions.because: one mechanism to shoot and climb saves space and lets the team focus on the shooter
decisions.instead_of: a separate scissor climber, smaller and lighter than a telescoping one
